Scanned all 264 packages of the twelve published builds (10.0.2-r0, 10.0.3-r0, 10.0.4-r0, 10.0.5-r0, 10.0.6-r0, 10.0.7-r0, 10.0.8-r0, 10.0.9-r0, 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold: every build ships Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel.Core.dll at its own .NET version, in the ASP.NET Core shared framework of aspnetcore10-runtime and of the .NET SDK held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap, and in the ASP.NET Core runtime pack and the ASP.NET Core runtime archive held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap; the other copies are reference assemblies with no implementation code. That version is 10.0.2 to 10.0.10 in the first nine builds and 10.0.13 or later from 10.0.13-r0 on. The range ends at 10.0.13-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-70186 (GHSA-mf4x-w4gh-4656) is an ASP.NET Core denial of service issue: crafted HTTP/3 reset or abort sequences can deadlock Kestrel connection handling and exhaust server resources. Microsoft lists the Linux ASP.NET Core runtime packs among the affected packages and fixed .NET 9 in 9.0.21 (https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/security/advisories/GHSA-mf4x-w4gh-4656, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/461, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.21/9.0.21.md). DHI dotnet9-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 9 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 242 packages of the eleven published builds (9.0.12-r0, 9.0.13-r0, 9.0.14-r0, 9.0.15-r0, 9.0.16-r0, 9.0.17-r0, 9.0.18-r0, 9.0.20-r0, 9.0.21-r0, 9.0.22-r0 and 9.0.23-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold: the ASP.NET Core shared framework ships in aspnetcore9-runtime, with further copies in the SDK held by dotnet9-runtime-bootstrap and in ASP.NET Core NuGet packages in dotnet9-runtime-artifacts. In every build and on both architectures, the copies of Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel.Core.dll, which holds Kestrel's HTTP/3 connection handling, in the ASP.NET Core shared frameworks, the runtime pack and the reference packs carry that build's ASP.NET Core version, as does the shared framework directory; the only copies at another version are metadata-only reference assemblies from the Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Ref 6.0.2 and 8.0.0 reference packages in dotnet9-runtime-artifacts, which hold no code. The copies at the build's version also carry the dotnet/dotnet source commit they were built from: in 9.0.20-r0 it is the v9.0.121 tag (https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/releases/tag/v9.0.121), which builds ASP.NET Core 9.0.20, and in 9.0.21-r0 it is the v9.0.122 tag (https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/releases/tag/v9.0.122), which builds ASP.NET Core 9.0.21 and is the first to contain Microsoft's fix, https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/commit/4919ba0124e081fd33e5bd66e825efb4f285509b (Fix h3 connection-level and stream-level abort locking), the only change to Kestrel's HTTP/3 code between ASP.NET Core 9.0.20 and 9.0.21. In 9.0.12-r0 through 9.0.20-r0 ASP.NET Core is 9.0.12 through 9.0.20, which are affected; from 9.0.21-r0 on, the version is 9.0.21 or later, with Microsoft's fix. The range ends at 9.0.21-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-70186 (GHSA-mf4x-w4gh-4656) is an ASP.NET Core denial of service issue in Kestrel (Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel.Core): an unauthenticated remote attacker can send crafted HTTP/3 reset or abort sequences that deadlock connection handling and exhaust server resources. Microsoft lists the ASP.NET Core 10.0 runtime packs, including linux-x64 and linux-arm64, as affected from 10.0.0 through 10.0.12 and fixed in 10.0.13: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mf4x-w4gh-4656, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/461, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.13/10.0.13.md. The only change to Kestrel's Internal/Http3 sources between the dotnet/dotnet v10.0.112 and v10.0.113 tags is dotnet/aspnetcore source update commit e598e941d3d0b974203382600fa48ae3b6e1adfc on release/10.0.1xx, which moves Http3Stream's abort side effects outside its completion lock and makes request finalization wait for an in-flight abort: https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/commit/e598e941d3d0b974203382600fa48ae3b6e1adfc. DHI dotnet-sdk-10 for Debian 13 packages Microsoft's .NET 10 SDK for Linux, which includes the .NET runtime and the ASP.NET Core shared framework. We scanned every package built from this source in the DHI Debian repository, 10.0.301-0, 10.0.302-0, 10.0.302-1, 10.0.400-1, 10.0.401-0, 10.0.401-1, 10.0.402-0, 10.0.403-0, 10.0.404-0 and 10.0.404-1, for amd64 and arm64 (the dotnet-sdk-10 and dotnet-sdk-10-oci-config packages; no debug-symbol packages are published), after verifying each against its index checksum and including the files inside the nupkg archives they hold. The dotnet-sdk-10-oci-config packages hold only an image configuration YAML file and a changelog. Every dotnet-sdk-10 build carries one implementation copy of Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel.Core.dll, in the ASP.NET Core shared framework under /usr/lib/dotnet/shared/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App/<version>, and one reference assembly with no implementation code under /usr/lib/dotnet/packs/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Ref/<version>; no other copy is present, including inside the nupkg archives. The shared framework version is 10.0.9 in 10.0.301-0, 10.0.10 in 10.0.302-0 and 10.0.302-1, 10.0.11 in 10.0.400-1, 10.0.12 in 10.0.401-0 and 10.0.401-1, 10.0.13 in 10.0.402-0, 10.0.14 in 10.0.403-0 and 10.0.15 in 10.0.404-0 and 10.0.404-1, the same on both architectures. Every copy records the dotnet/dotnet commit it was built from: the v10.0.109 to v10.0.112 tags in the builds up to 10.0.401-1, and the v10.0.113, v10.0.114 and v10.0.115 tags from 10.0.402-0 on, all three of which contain the fix commit. The range ends at 10.0.402-0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

The product version of every implementation copy names the dotnet/aspnetcore release commit it was built from: the v8.0.28 to v8.0.31 tag commits in the builds up to 8.0.425-1, and the v8.0.32, v8.0.33 and v8.0.34 tag commits from 8.0.426-0 on, all three of which contain the fix commit. CVE-2026-70186 (GHSA-mf4x-w4gh-4656) is an ASP.NET Core denial of service issue in Kestrel (Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel.Core): an unauthenticated remote attacker can send crafted HTTP/3 reset or abort sequences that deadlock connection handling and exhaust server resources. Microsoft lists the ASP.NET Core 8.0 runtime packs, including linux-x64 and linux-arm64, as affected from 8.0.0 through 8.0.31 and fixed in 8.0.32: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mf4x-w4gh-4656, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/461, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.32/8.0.32.md. The .NET 8 fix is dotnet/aspnetcore commit 1fa2d2575e43732eb49dbb800d64a3202857ea33 on release/8.0 ('Fix h3 connection-level and stream-level abort locking'), which changes Http3Stream.cs; it is in the v8.0.32, v8.0.33 and v8.0.34 tags and not in v8.0.31: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/commit/1fa2d2575e43732eb49dbb800d64a3202857ea33. DHI dotnet-sdk-8 for Debian 13 packages Microsoft's prebuilt .NET 8 SDK for Linux, which includes the .NET runtime and the ASP.NET Core shared framework. We scanned every package built from this source that the DHI Debian repository published as of 2026-11-27, 8.0.422-0, 8.0.423-0, 8.0.423-1, 8.0.424-1, 8.0.425-0, 8.0.425-1, 8.0.426-0, 8.0.427-0, 8.0.428-0 and 8.0.428-1, for amd64 and arm64 (the dotnet-sdk-8 and dotnet-sdk-8-oci-config packages; no debug-symbol packages are published), after checking each against its index checksum. We read the file list and checksums of all 20 dotnet-sdk-8 packages, and unpacked 19 of them (all but the arm64 8.0.422-0 package) to read the version resources of every copy of the affected assemblies, including any inside the nupkg archives the packages hold (none of those archives contains one). The arm64 8.0.422-0 package is placed from its file list, which has the same copies at the same paths under 8.0.28 shared framework directories; it sits below the boundary either way. The dotnet-sdk-8-oci-config packages hold only an image configuration YAML file and a changelog. Every dotnet-sdk-8 build carries one implementation copy of Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel.Core.dll, in the ASP.NET Core shared framework under /usr/lib/dotnet/shared/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App/<version>, and one reference assembly with no implementation code under /usr/lib/dotnet/packs/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Ref/<version>; there is no other copy. The shared framework version is 8.0.28 in 8.0.422-0, 8.0.29 in 8.0.423-0 and 8.0.423-1, 8.0.30 in 8.0.424-1, 8.0.31 in 8.0.425-0 and 8.0.425-1, 8.0.32 in 8.0.426-0, 8.0.33 in 8.0.427-0 and 8.0.34 in 8.0.428-0 and 8.0.428-1, the same on both architectures (8.0.422-0 arm64 from its file list). The product version of every implementation copy names the dotnet/aspnetcore release commit it was built from: the v8.0.28 to v8.0.31 tag commits in the builds up to 8.0.425-1, and the v8.0.32, v8.0.33 and v8.0.34 tag commits from 8.0.426-0 on, all three of which contain the fix commit. The range ends at 8.0.426-0 because it is the first published build with the fix.
